root_idea.summary: The root centers on straying away and separation, especially the flight or dispersal of an animal or group.
root_idea.development: From physical fleeing and dispersal, the semantic field extends to opposition: a nidd is a counterpart that takes a different course or stands against another. Some associated words preserve the meanings of gathering, raised calling, and other specialized lexical developments.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is the plural أَندَاد; the public headword is normalized to the singular dictionary citation form نِدّ.

senses.definition: A counterpart or equal sharing the essential nature of another.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural أنداد, the word denotes supposed counterparts or equals attributed to Allah; the emphasis is on likeness or equivalence rather than similarity in any incidental respect.

senses.definition: A rival or opposing counterpart, including a substitute set up in another’s place.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, أنداد refers to beings or idols treated as rivals to Allah or taken as objects of worship instead of Him; this polemical use explains translations such as “rivals.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take fright, shy, bolt, or run away wildly; to become refractory and go off at random.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a camel or other animal that breaks loose and flees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assemble, said of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate reported usage of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deviate from the established course of speech, said of a word.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a less authoritative usage and compared with شذّ.
The usage can involve loudly saying about another person something that he dislikes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To expose or proclaim another’s faults, making him notorious or infamous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with بِهِ; applicable in verse or prose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone hear foul or abusive speech; to revile him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A stronger abusive use related to loudly denouncing the person addressed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To oppose or contend against someone; to argue against him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction with a personal object.
A Form IV usage applied to a herd or group of camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disperse themselves and go away in different directions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression يَوْمُ التَّنَادِّ, this is interpreted as the day of people’s dispersal at the Resurrection; the same expression was also explained as the day of their assembling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fumigating perfume or aromatic substance, including a fragrant wood or compound perfume.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical identification varies among authorities, with proposed associations including ghaliyah, ambergris, and other perfumes; its Arabic authenticity is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A high hill rising toward the sky; a great hill of clay or loam.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a dialectal usage of Yemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel prone to taking fright, shying, and running away at random.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival noun describing the animal’s recurrent disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One that takes fright, shies, and runs away at random; a bolting camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is نِدَاد; نَدَد is also used as a quasi-plural for camels in a state of dispersion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have no means of subsistence or livelihood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom apparently refers to the absence of livestock or other live stock, drawing on the sense of a camel that has bolted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dispersed in separate directions, said of birds or of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expressions describe a scattered group; variant forms include يَنَادِيد and تَنَادِيد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A voice raised high in calling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of a loudly raised calling voice.
